policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Select A, move to the top of the visible button to prepare, only when the observed hand is not already prepared. Recognize a closed gripper with wrist height approximately 0.15 (including 0.154–0.155), wrist roughly 34–36 image units above the button, and a small horizontal offset as already prepared. This configuration takes precedence over apparent wrist/button image-center misalignment: the wrist is not the fingertips' contact point. Do not select A merely because those image centers differ. Once prepared, choose between B and C using the updated passage_count and the requested ordinal N from the goal. C must be initiated before the requested passage because button pressing takes approximately 25–35 recording time units. For a prepared hand, select C only when both conditions hold: the updated passage_count equals N-1, and a reliable crossing-time calculation gives 0 < estimated remaining arrival time <= 35 recording time units. An estimate above 35 is outside the launch window; do not round it into the window. The count alone never authorizes C. Select B if passage_count is less than N-1, or if it equals N-1 but the estimated next passage is outside this window or its timing is uncertain. Estimate the upcoming arrival using incoming motion_history together with all newly shown execution observations, accounting for slowing and reversal at endpoints. Calculate the next crossing timestamp before choosing C. First check the combined timestamped evidence for repeated motion: matching positions and directions across cycles can establish a period. When recurrence is established, interpolate earlier crossings of the currently visible target x between their bracketing samples and advance those crossing times by whole periods. Use the earliest predicted crossing strictly after the current timestamp, considering both crossing directions. Prefer this observed recurrence over a conflicting rough velocity estimate. If recurrence is not yet established, fit smooth periodic motion x(t)=a+b*cos(w*t)+c*sin(w*t) to the combined timestamped evidence, allowing for pixel noise, and solve for its earliest crossing of the currently visible target x strictly after the current timestamp. If neither method reliably establishes whether arrival is within the launch window, select B. Earlier travel and reversal evidence must continue to inform the estimate when the newest interval is short or nearly stationary. Do not extrapolate a near-zero endpoint velocity as constant or interpret two identical endpoint positions as evidence that the cube has permanently stopped. From the combined timestamped evidence, estimate the next target-crossing timestamp and subtract the current timestamp to obtain the remaining arrival time. Apply this calculation after an observed reversal as well as during approach to or departure from an endpoint; retain earlier travel and reversal evidence in the estimate. If the hand is prepared, updated passage_count=N-1, and the evidence reliably establishes 0 < estimated remaining arrival time <= 35 recording time units, select C. This conjunction requires C, rather than merely permitting it. Choose B if the crossing is farther away or the combined evidence genuinely cannot establish whether it is within the window; endpoint proximity alone still never authorizes C. Update crossing counts only from newly shown observations, never by recounting retained history. When the cube is moving away from the target after the preceding crossing, calculate the next crossing by including both the remaining travel to the endpoint and the return travel to the target; distance to the target divided by current speed is not a valid arrival estimate in this situation. Slowing down or nearing an endpoint does not by itself authorize C. A fast endpoint turnaround can nevertheless be the press-launch time if the estimated next crossing is within the lead window and passage_count equals N-1; do not require that the cube already be moving toward the target. Select B while fewer than N-1 passages have completed, or while the requested next passage remains farther away than this lead window. Reevaluate after every B; remaining static can span several passages, so update memory from every shown frame. None of these menu options requires a supplied point; A and C concern the visible button. Use the timing-uncertainty fallback to B only when the combined motion evidence genuinely cannot establish whether arrival is within the lead window. Pixel noise or modest uncertainty in the exact crossing timestamp does not justify waiting when the well-supported arrival estimates lie wholly within that window and the preparedness and ordinal conditions hold; select C in that case. Otherwise refine the estimate from the next observations rather than pressing on the wrong ordinal. If already stopped at the requested target, remain static. For other uncovered situations, prepare with A if necessary, otherwise remain static with B.

fields.name: passage_count
fields.description: Start at 0 for empty memory, otherwise use the incoming passage_count. Process all newly shown observations chronologically, starting with incoming last_side as the preceding side. Compute the sign of cube x minus target x. Each nonzero sign opposite to the preceding nonzero side increments the count once; then update the working side. Ignore exact equality until a nonzero side appears. Include observations during A and B, and count multiple crossings within one decision interval separately. Write the resulting count, without adding any predicted future passage from the command being selected. e.g. 2

fields.name: last_side
fields.description: The cube's most recently observed nonzero side of the target center, represented as -1 when cube x is smaller than target x and 1 when it is larger. If exactly equal, retain the preceding nonzero side; use 0 if none has yet been observed. Record the side at the decision's final observation, not the side expected after its selected command. e.g. -1

fields.name: motion_history
fields.description: With empty memory, start with an empty ordered list; otherwise preserve incoming motion_history. Append all newly shown execution observations chronologically, including the final observation, keeping only one sample for any repeated timestamp. Exclude demonstration observations. Write only observed timestamps and cube x measurements, never predicted positions or command outcomes. Use the combined incoming history and newly shown execution observations to estimate motion for subgoal selection. Do not recount retained history when updating passage_count: that update still uses only newly shown observations and incoming last_side. Each history entry contains a timestamp and a scalar cube x measurement, not a spatial coordinate pair. Serialize the field as list text with single-quoted keys, key order 'time' then 'cube_x', and one space after each colon and comma. Do not include extra outer quotation marks within the value. Use [] for an empty list. This representation does not change the observations retained. e.g. [{'time': 0, 'cube_x': 47}, {'time': 16, 'cube_x': 80}, {'time': 32, 'cube_x': 147}]
